later_events.mechanism: partial supersession of EO 10738 by EO 10906 (State-official inspection of estate and gift-tax returns made under the 1939 or 1954 Code), effective on filing for publication on 1961-01-18 (filing line F.R. Doc. 61-564, Jan. 18, 1961, at offset 3374 of the held text; effectiveness paragraph at offsets 2872-3350); not an end of the whole clause

amendment by EO 10954 (signed 1961-07-26) of the supersession paragraph of EO 10906 so that it covers only estate and gift-tax returns made under the 1954 Code, effective as of 1961-01-18; leaves 1939-Code returns under EO 10738; not an end

clauses.mechanism: express revocation by EO 12553 (table of revoked orders; effective on signing, February 25, 1986, no effective-date wording)
clauses.reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 708-1702 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10738.txt, 22 FR 9205): signed 1957-11-15; orders that any estate or gift tax return made under the Internal Revenue Code of 1939 or the Internal Revenue Code of 1954 be open to inspection by any official, body or commission lawfully charged with the administration of any State tax law, in accordance with the Treasury regulations and decision it names, and states that the order is effective upon its filing for publication in the Federal Register. Later partial events, recorded as later events and not as the end: (1) Executive Order 10906, signed 1961-01-17 and filed 1961-01-18 (F.R. Doc. 61-564, filing line at offset 3374 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_10906.txt; its paragraph on effectiveness is at offsets 2872-3350), became effective on filing and on that date superseded EO 10738 to the extent applicable to inspection by State tax officials, after the effective date, of estate and gift-tax returns made under the 1939 or 1954 Code; (2) Executive Order 10954, signed 1961-07-26, replaced that paragraph with a version limited to returns made under the 1954 Code and provided that it is effective as of 1961-01-18. After EO 10954 the supersession reaches only 1954-Code returns, so the command continued for estate and gift tax returns made under the 1939 Code (the amendment is retroactive to the same day, so the net effect from 1961-01-18 is a supersession limited to 1954-Code returns). The clause therefore continued in part after 1961 and ended as a whole only when revoked. A possible earlier statutory extinguishment through later rewriting of Internal Revenue Code section 6103 is not shown by any held source and is not relied on. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986), which orders that the Executive Orders in its table, and any amendments thereto, are revoked. The number 10738 appears in the table's column of order numbers at offset 10632 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt (the held OCR prints the numbers and the subjects in separate blocks, so identification rests on the number). EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, February 25, 1986; the filing date (2-26-86) and the printing date are not effective dates. EO 12553 has no exception text, so the revocation reaches the remaining 1939-Code portion.

research_rationale:
EO 10738 is a one-paragraph authorization for State tax officials to inspect estate and gift tax returns. EO 10906 (effective 1961-01-18 on filing) superseded it for State-official inspection of returns made under the 1939 and 1954 Codes, and EO 10954 (effective as of 1961-01-18) narrowed that supersession to 1954-Code returns, leaving 1939-Code returns under EO 10738. Both are recorded as partial later events. The whole clause ended on the express revocation by EO 12553 on 1986-02-25 (signature date, no effective-date wording). Searches: the U.S. Code and eCFR searches record two citation hits each for this order without a located text slice in the dossier, so they were not treated as evidence of continuation; the OFR disposition-note search lists the three chain events.
